Your Spear tower has reached level 10 (or Spike tower level 20) and can now build barricades!
Barricades are wooden structures placed on adjacent path tiles that block enemy movement.
Spear tower barricades have HP = level - 10 (minimum 1). Spike tower barricades have HP = (level - 20) / 2 (minimum 1).
When enemies reach a barricade, they attack it with damage equal to their level (dragons deal 5× their level).
If a barricade is destroyed, the enemy moves to that tile.
You can build new barricades or reinforce existing ones, and click on barricades to remove them.

Your Spike tower has reached level 10 and now has barbs!
When a level 10+ Spike tower attacks an enemy, it reduces the enemy's movement by 1 tile per attack.
This effect stacks - multiple attacks from any level 10+ Spike towers will further reduce enemy movement.
Enemies will always move at least 1 tile per turn, even with multiple barb effects.

Your tower has reached level 20 and now has an extended area attack! Fireball and acid attacks now affect enemies within 2 tiles of the target instead of just 1 tile. This makes your area attacks much more powerful against groups of enemies!

The Wizard Tower is a powerful area-of-effect tower that launches fireballs at enemies!
Each fireball damages the target and all enemies in adjacent tiles.
It has a longer build time (2 turns) but can devastate groups of enemies.
At level 10, wizards can place magical traps that teleport enemies back to spawn.
At level 20, the fireball radius increases to 2 tiles!

The Alchemy Tower throws acid that deals damage over time!
Unlike other towers, acid damage persists for multiple rounds (base 2 turns, increases with level).
The acid affects the target and adjacent enemies in a small area.
While the damage per turn is lower, the total damage over time can be very effective.
At level 20, the acid area increases to 2 tiles!

The Ballista is a long-range siege weapon with exceptional range (5 tiles) and high damage!
However, it has a minimum range of 3 tiles and cannot attack nearby enemies.
It requires 2 turns to build.
Use it to target enemies from a distance before they get too close, or position it behind other towers for maximum effectiveness.

The Dwarven Mine is a special structure that generates coins through mining operations!
Unlike combat towers, mines use the "dig" action to find valuable resources (rubble, brass, silver, gold, gems, or diamonds).
Mines can also build traps that damage enemies.
At higher levels, mines can dig more times per turn and reach further.
Warning: Dragons are greedy and will destroy mines to claim the treasure!
You can place towers on river tiles! When you do, they will be placed on rafts.
Rafts move automatically with the river flow at the end of each turn. The flow speed determines how many tiles they move (1 or 2 tiles).
Rafts are destroyed if they reach a maelstrom (whirlpool) or move out of the map boundaries. The tower on the raft is also destroyed.
Bridges block raft movement. Rafts cannot pass through bridges spanning the river. Multiple rafts on the same river move in order - downstream rafts move first.
Dwarven mines cannot be placed on river tiles. Mines require solid ground and cannot be built on rafts. Please select a build area on land instead.
The Green Witch can heal other enemies! At the end of each enemy turn, she heals all adjacent enemies by 5 times her level (e.g., level 2 witch heals 10 HP per turn).
She will move towards Ewhad if he has damaged health to heal him. Focus on defeating the Green Witch quickly or she will make battles much harder!
The Red Witch can disable your towers! She disables the nearest ready tower of her level or lower for 3 turns.
Disabled towers cannot attack and show "Disabled: XT" in their info panel. Upgrade your towers to higher levels or defeat the Red Witch quickly!

Welcome to the Level Editor! This tool allows you to create custom maps, levels, and level sequences for Defender of Egril.

To add new levels to the game: First, select or create a map in the Map Editor. Then, create a level using that map in the Level Editor. Finally, bind the level on the World Map to make it visible and playable in the game.
You can copy existing maps and levels and adapt them to create new content quickly. This is a great way to learn and iterate on your designs.

The Restore Game Data button in Settings restores the game data from the game\'s own repository (stored locally, not online). When you use this function, your previous version with any user changes will be saved under a new name in the same folder, so your work is preserved.
All editor data is stored in JSON format on your local filesystem:
maps/ - Contains all map definitions - levels/ - Contains all level definitions - sequence.json - Defines level order - worldmap.json - Defines world map positions
The Map Editor lets you create the grid layout for your levels. Maps define the hexagonal grid, spawn points, paths, and build areas where towers can be placed.

Select and place tile types (PATH, BUILD_AREA, ISLAND, NO_PLAY, SPAWN_POINT, TARGET, RIVER) - Paint tiles by clicking or dragging - Configure river properties (flow direction and speed) - Zoom in/out with Ctrl+Scroll or zoom buttons - Collapse the header for more editing space - Change all NO_PLAY tiles to PATH at once
The Level Editor lets you create gameplay levels using existing maps. Each level references a map and defines the enemies, resources, and available towers.

Select a map for your level - Set starting coins and health points - Configure enemy spawns by turn - Choose which tower types are available - Add spawn points and waypoints - Configure tower restrictions and special rules
The Level Sequence tab lets you arrange levels in the order they appear in the game. This defines the progression and difficulty curve.
Drag and drop levels to reorder - Use up and down buttons to move levels - Add levels to the sequence - Remove levels from the sequence - Set level dependencies
The World Map Positions tab lets you define where levels appear on the world map and how they are connected.

Set X/Y coordinates for each level - Create connections between levels (road or sea) - Auto-connect levels based on dependencies - Configure connection visual styles - Define waypoints for connection paths

Save frequently to avoid losing work - Test your levels in the game to ensure they are balanced - Use the existing levels as templates - Maps can be reused across multiple levels - The sequence determines which levels are playable

When you open the game, start a level, or finish a level (by winning, losing, or leaving), an event is sent to the game's own server.
Each event records the server date and time, the game version, and the platform you are using (desktop, mobile, or web).
If you are logged in, your username is also saved together with the event.
A pseudonymous install ID, which gives no information about the user, is generated and added to the event logging.
This is to see how many users we have and if there are levels where users get stuck.
Otherwise, events are fully anonymous — no username, user ID, or IP address is logged.
When a level ends (won, lost, or left), the current turn number is also recorded.

This data is used to understand how many people play the game and to identify levels that may be too difficult.
No data is shared with third parties.
If you play offline, the logging calls fail silently — the game works completely without internet access.

An account is entirely optional — you can play the full game without registering. With a free account you can:

• Save your game progress on the server and continue on any device
• Switch between desktop, mobile, and web — and resume exactly where you left off
• Upload your own custom maps and levels as community content for others to discover and play
• Download and play levels created by other players

Click the login button on the start page. A login code and URL will appear — open the URL in a browser (on your phone or any other device) and enter the code to log in or create a free account. Only an e-mail address is required.

Note: Keyboard shortcuts are available on desktop and in the web app.

Use Tab / Shift+Tab to cycle through available tower types. The highlighted type is shown in the buy panel. Click a green tile on the map to place the tower. Use Ctrl+Enter to start the battle when ready.

Use Tab to jump to the next actionable tower. An auto-target is highlighted. Press F or Enter to attack. Press U to upgrade, X to undo/sell (with confirmation). Use M to open the spell menu, then Tab/Shift+Tab to select a spell and Enter to cast it. Press T to return to tower mode. Use Ctrl+Enter to end the turn.
Use W/A/S/D (or arrow keys) to pan the map. Use R to center on the selected tower, G to center on the next spawn point. Mouse scroll or pinch to zoom.

The tyrannical warchief who united the Orks and Ogres under his banner, a massive colossus clad in black iron.
His War Cry drives nearby Horde units into a frenzy, letting them advance faster. Cut him down before his roar overwhelms your defenses!
Gribnak the Squealer enters the battlefield
Gribnak the Squealer has entered the battlefield!
This Snotling Chieftain will summon many small snotlings around his position.
He summons increasingly powerful Demons, and if he reaches the target the battle is lost instantly. Bring him down fast before his host overwhelms your defenses!
Morguk Bonewhisper, Goblin Shaman of the Bonewhisper clan, has entered the battlefield!

His War Totem Aura hastens nearby goblins, his Hex of Silence disables towers, and every few turns Spirit Summon calls new goblins on adjacent tiles.\nTake him down before his rituals overwhelm your defenses!
A brilliant but utterly insane goblin inventor riding a steam-powered mechanical spider has entered the battlefield.
He periodically drops scrap piles that hatch into robotic goblins, each with reinforced metal bodies. He launches rockets that stun towers at long range.
Fallen Shieldmaiden Freya enters the battlefield
Once a heroic shieldmaiden, Freya fell in battle and rose again as an unstoppable death knight wrapped in black steel and grave magic.

Her Shield Wall blocks all non-ballista attacks from the front for her own tile and the tiles to her left and right as she advances. Strike from the side or rear, or shoot over the shield with a Ballista, before the undead champion crushes your line.
Prince Valerius the Soulreaper enters the battlefield
Prince Valerius the Soulreaper, an ancient lich and ruler of the skeleton armies, steps onto the battlefield in a wave of icy grave-cold.

His Soul Call raises nearby fallen allies at the start of the next round. The living return as zombies, the undead rise again as skeletons, and even dragons can return as undead dragons. Destroy him quickly before every casualty strengthens his host.
Soul Call: nearby dead allies rise next round
Silas the Maskmaster enters the battlefield
Silas the Maskmaster, a wandering illusionist wrapped in velvet and lies, has stepped onto the battlefield.

Periodically he creates mirror images on nearby path tiles. Only the real Silas can be hurt; when a tower strikes an illusion, the image vanishes and that tower is blinded for a few rounds. Silas may swap places with his fresh doubles the moment they appear, so watch carefully before you fire!
The tower struck only a mirror image of Silas. The illusion shattered, but the attacking tower is now blinded for a few rounds and cannot attack.
Grand Coven-Mother Sybilla enters the battlefield
The most powerful witch in the coven has arrived! Grand Coven-Mother Sybilla commands the full might of the Witch Coven — and she brings the twins Haga and Zussa with her.

Always arrives with twins Haga and Zussa. Coven Synergy: nearby green witches heal allies more strongly, while nearby red witches keep towers disabled for longer. She also supports the coven with healing and disruptive magic, and she can swap places with a nearby witch to keep her enemies guessing.
Haga the Healing Twin enters the battlefield
Haga, the elder of Sybilla\'s unequal twins, steps onto the field. Where her magic flows, wounded allies are restored far faster than any ordinary healer could manage.

The Level Editor lets you create custom maps, levels, and sequences for Defender of Egril. It has four main tabs: Map Editor, Level Editor, Level Sequence, and World Map Positions. Use this guide to learn how to use each one.

1. Create or select a map in the Map Editor tab - 2. Create a level in the Level Editor tab that uses that map - 3. Test your level by playing it in the game - Note: Steps 4 and 5 are only required for official levels shipped with the game; user-created and community levels are playable without them - 4. (Official levels only) Add the level to the sequence in the Level Sequence tab - 5. (Official levels only) Place and connect the level on the World Map Positions tab

Design the hexagonal tile layout for your level. Select an existing map from the list to edit it, or click "New Map" to create a blank map. Give the map a name, set its width and height, then paint tiles to build your terrain.

PATH: The route enemies walk along - BUILD_AREA: Areas where towers can be placed (adjacent to PATH tiles, auto-calculated) - ISLAND: A 2×2 build area in the middle of paths - NO_PLAY: Non-playable background area (default for unset tiles) - SPAWN_POINT: Where enemies enter the map - TARGET: The goal enemies try to reach - RIVER: Water tile with a configurable flow direction and speed

Click a tile to paint it with the selected tile type - Click and drag to paint multiple tiles at once - Ctrl+Scroll or the zoom buttons to zoom in and out - Click the collapse/expand button to collapse or expand the header for more editing space - "Change All NO_PLAY to PATH" converts every background tile to PATH at once
Select the RIVER tile type, then configure the flow direction (e.g. NORTH, EAST, SOUTH_WEST) and flow speed using the controls that appear. River tiles are visual only and do not affect gameplay.

Create gameplay levels using existing maps. Select a level from the list to edit it, or click "New Level" to create one. Each level has five configuration sub-tabs shown at the top of the editing view.

Title: The level name displayed on the world map - Subtitle: Optional short description shown below the title - Author: Your name or handle - Map: Select which map this level uses - Start Coins: The coins the player begins with - Start Health Points: The lives the player starts with - Test Level: Hides the level from normal gameplay (useful for testing) - Allow Auto-Attack: Lets towers attack automatically without player input

Define which enemies appear during the level and when. Click "Add Enemy" to add a new entry. For each spawn, select the enemy type, set its level (higher level scales health), choose the turn number when it appears, and optionally pick the spawn point on the map. A red badge on the tab means required information is missing.

Choose which tower types are available to the player in this level. Toggle each tower type on or off using the checkboxes. At least one tower must be enabled – a red badge appears on the tab if no towers are selected.

Waypoints define intermediate or branching points on enemy paths between spawn points and the target. Click "Add Waypoint" to add a new waypoint, set its grid position, and link it to a spawn point or another waypoint to form a path chain. The minimap shows all waypoint positions relative to the map. A red badge means the waypoint configuration is incomplete or invalid.

Pre-place towers on the map before the player starts the level. Select a tower type from the list, then click a tile on the minimap to place it there. Click an already-placed tower to remove it. This is useful for tutorial levels or levels that begin with pre-built defenses.

The Level Sequence defines the order in which official levels appear in the game and sets their dependencies. This tab is not needed for user-created or community levels, which are managed separately and always accessible from the world map.

Use the up and down buttons to reorder levels in the sequence - Levels are linked by dependency: a level is unlocked when its predecessor is completed - The sequence is saved to sequence.json - Only levels in the sequence appear in the game
World Map Positions Tab (Official Levels Only)

Place official levels on the visual world map and define the connections between them. User-created and community levels do not need to be placed here – they are always accessible via the dedicated user/community level panels on the world map.

Each entry represents a level location on the world map image - Set X/Y pixel coordinates to position the location on the map - Add connections between locations to link them visually - Choose the connection type: Road (land path) or Sea Route (ocean path) - Add control points to curve a connection line between two locations - The minimap shows a preview of all locations and connections

Save frequently to avoid losing work - Test your levels by playing the game after each change - Copy existing maps and levels as starting templates to learn the format - A map can be reused across multiple levels - Red badges on sub-tabs indicate missing or invalid configuration - The "Restore Game Data" button in Settings resets all official content to its original state

Create a free Egril account to save your progress in the cloud and continue playing on any device. Tap the player name at the top to log in or sign up.
With an Egril account your saves sync across desktop, mobile and web. Use Save in-game and Load Game on the world map to pick up where you left off.
Most actions have keyboard shortcuts. Open Settings to view and customize them. Turn on "Show shortcut chips" to see the key for each button right on its label.
Win battles to earn XP and ability points. Spend ability points on spells (like Fireball or Healing) that you can cast during battle.
Spend ability points on Construction abilities to unlock new tower types and upgrades, expanding the defenses you can build.
Ability points also unlock passive perks: faster gold gain, cheaper towers, stronger barricades and more. Browse the Abilities screen to plan your build.
Leveling up a tower extends its attack range, letting it strike enemies further along the path.
Some towers gain extra attacks per turn when leveled up — namely the Spike and Spear towers. More actions means more damage output per round.
Every tower upgrade adds damage. Investing coins in upgrades is often more effective than building another low-level tower of the same type.
High-level towers can place Barricades on neighboring tiles, blocking enemy paths and forcing them onto longer routes through your defenses.

Barricade HP scales with the building tower\'s level. Enemies reaching a barricade attack it for damage equal to their level (dragons hit much harder!). Reinforce key barricades by building on the same tile, or click one to remove it.
High-level Wizard towers can deploy Magical Traps. When an enemy steps on a trap, it is teleported back to its spawn point — great for buying time at chokepoints during tough waves.
The Dwarven Mine generates coins through digging. It deals no damage, but a mine pays for several extra towers each level.
Dwarven Mines and dragons don\'t mix: greedy dragons hunt mines down to claim the treasure, and digging too deep can even summon a new dragon. Plan ahead before sinking lots of coins into mines.
Build towers right on the river using Barges — any tower works except the Dwarven Mine, which needs solid ground. Barges drift along the water flow each turn, so their position keeps changing.
Place towers on Build Areas next to the path. Towers cover hexagonal tiles within their range, so corners and bends are excellent spots for maximum coverage.
Mix tower types: cheap Spike towers slow enemies in melee while Bow and Ballista towers pick them off from afar. Layered defenses are far stronger than a single tower type.
Wizard towers deal area-of-effect damage. Place them where enemies bunch up — near spawn points or behind barricades — to hit multiple targets at once.
The Ballista has a minimum range of 3 — it cannot hit enemies right next to it. Pair it with melee towers (Spike, Spear) to cover the close-range gap.
Some enemies are immune to certain attacks: Red Demons resist fireballs, Blue Demons resist acid. Watch the upcoming wave and bring a varied set of towers.
Preview: The First Villains Enter the Battlefield!

Get ready for a new challenge! With the upcoming update, **Villains** are coming to Defender of Egril.

### What Are Villains?

Villains are powerful boss enemies that appear at the head of enemy waves. They are significantly tougher than regular foes and possess unique abilities that will put your defenses to the test: they stun towers, call for reinforcements, or shield the troops that follow. Defeating them requires more than raw firepower – you'll need to adapt your strategy!

---

### First Look: These Villains Await You at the Start

* **Baron Rattlejaw (Goblin Inventor):** A mad inventor riding a mighty spider machine. He drops wreckage that spawns robot goblins and knocks out your towers with targeted rockets.
* **The Fallen Shield-Maiden Freya (Death Knight):** Once an undefeatable warrior. With her magical shield wall, she absorbs frontal tower damage for herself and the units behind her.
* **Prince Valerius the Soul Reaper (Skeleton Lord):** An ancient lich and ruler of the undead. As long as he stands on the field, he transforms every defeated enemy nearby into an undead minion.
* **Captain Roderich (The Buccaneer):** Appears on maps with waterways and takes targeted shots at your rafts. Defeat him and claim his pirate treasure!

*Prepare your towers – soon you'll need to prove whether your defenses can withstand the first powerful villains!*

Fast and nimble, goblins are the weakest enemies but move quickly. Use area attacks to handle multiple goblins at once.
Muscular and tough, Orks are the standard Horde infantry. They move slower than goblins but pack more health and damage.
Massive and powerful, Ogres are formidable enemies with high health. Despite their size, they can be extremely dangerous in groups.

A creature of stone immune to blade attacks — melee and ranged towers deal no damage. Only fire and acid can harm it. The Troll moves every other turn and tramples smaller enemies. It destroys barricades with tremendous force.

Shambling undead reanimated by dark magic. Slower than skeletons but still dangerous in numbers, especially when healed by Green Witches.
A magic user who channels destructive spells from the air. Defeat them quickly before they rain fire upon your defenses.
A fast demon that thrives in acidic environments — it is immune to acid damage. Dispose of it with fire, physical attacks, or magical spells.

An ethereal undead spirit that floats over terrain obstacles. It resists non-magical attacks — only magical tower attacks like fireballs can harm it directly.

A dark magic user who can disable your towers for several turns, rendering them helpless. Prioritize defeating her to restore your defenses.

A small, weak minion summoned by goblin shamans. While individually harmless, they can become dangerous in large numbers.

An ancient and mighty creature with immense power. The Dragon flies after its first turn, moving faster and becoming even more dangerous.
A reanimated dragon cursed to eternal servitude. It possesses the same fearsome power as the living dragon but carries the curse of undeath.
